ai.title: e2e test files converted to ES modules
ai.summary: Added `export {}` to `store-hydration.spec.ts` and `store-ssr.spec.ts` in `web/src/__tests__/e2e/`. This marks the files as ES modules, resolving TypeScript compatibility issues with global scope detection. Scope limited to web e2e test infrastructure.

eli5.text: Two of the tests that check how the app's data store behaves during server-side loading and page hydration got a small tweak: they now explicitly identify themselves as ES modules by including a single `export {}` statement at the top of each file. This wasn't needed for regular feature code, but it fixes a compatibility issue where TypeScript couldn't properly detect the file's scope when running under the test tooling, which could cause confusing errors or silent failures during test runs. If you ran these specific end-to-end tests locally or in CI, you'd have seen them start passing (or stop erroring out) now that TypeScript recognizes them as proper modules instead of treating them as legacy script files with an implicit global scope.

ai.title: web: exclude Bun-only tests from Jest
ai.summary: Added playwright-runner.test.ts and ban-conditions.test.ts to testPathIgnorePatterns in web/jest.config.cjs. These tests rely on Bun-specific features and fail in the Jest environment. Scope limited to web package configuration.

eli5.text: Two specific test checks that were written to run only under the Bun environment have been added to the ignore list of the Jest test runner used by the web package. This means that when the web test suite is run with Jest, those two test files will be skipped entirely instead of failing. The change is live as part of this configuration update.
